text:
maya: Heads up — over the past ~6h rack15 (SXM3) has ~120 Xid/ECC events, most during long-seq training jobs. ECC correctable counters creeping up after ~24h uptime. Opening thread to triage. :eyes:

jon: Do we have a Grafana dashboard link? can we plot ECC/correctable vs uptime?

maya: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/rack15/gpu-metrics (quick snapshot attached in alert)

infra-bot: alert: rack15-gpu-pool XID/ECC spike (sev:medium) — 114 events in 6h across 9 nodes

suhas: Quick dump from one affected node (rack15-gpu-04):
```
[2026-03-18 10:12:34] Xid 79 pci_reset detected
GPU serial: SN-A1234-BATCH5
FW: 54.1.0.2
ECC correctable: 142 -> 310 (6h)
PCI link state flapping observed (retries)
```

alex: Batch number looks suspicious — BATCH5 was in the last A100 order in Dec. IIRC vendor flagged a few serial ranges earlier.

maya: Agreed. Pattern: same batch prefix (SN-A12xx) on 7/9 impacted cards. Full list: SN-A1234-BATCH5, SN-A1235-BATCH5, SN-A1240-BATCH5...

jon: Proposal: immediate mitigations
- cordon+drain the 8 most noisy GPUs overnight (low traffic window)
- move jobs to dedicated spare pool (spare-gpu-pool-usw2)
- enable aggressive ECC monitoring and auto-alert for Xid>5/min

ops-oncall: Draining 8 GPUs will reduce us-west-2 throughput ~12%. We have burst spare capacity in dedicated pool but it costs ~1.8x per-token. Need signoff for cost delta.

suhas: For triage, run these checks on each suspect node:
```
# quick health probe
kubectl exec -it -n infra gpu-health -- ./gpu-health-check --serial SN-A1234-BATCH5 --full-report > /tmp/gpu-SN-A1234.log
# grab dmesg + nvidia logs
journalctl -u nvidia-driver -b --no-pager | tail -n 200 > /tmp/nvidia-dmesg.log
```

maya: Also confirm if it's correlated with long seq (>=2048) or specific model sizes. Early signal showed most Xid spikes during 8k+ token runs.

alex: Re: vendor RMA — I'm opening a support ticket. Will attach serial list and logs. ETA for vendor triage is 48-72h. I'll request expedited RMA for nodes with repeated PCI resets.

jon: Any firmware changes recently?

maya: We rolled driverFW 54.1.0.2 to these racks on 2026-03-05. Non-impacted racks are still on 54.0.x. Could be FW regression or coincidental batch hardware issue.

suhas: Can we test rollback on a single node? Risk: rolling back driver/fw on-prod may require reboots and will disrupt running jobs. Suggest picking one low-util node in canary pool.

ops-oncall: I can coordinate a canary during 0200-0400 UTC window. We'll notify users.

infra-bot: scheduled: drain initiated for rack15-gpu-04 at 2026-03-19T02:15:00Z by ops-oncall

maya: After draining 04, we ran stress/memtest overnight. Results: intermittent ECC correctables still accumulate but no hard Xid crashes after migrate. Suggests degraded card rather than pure FW.

alex: Vendor response: "We're seeing a known silicon margin issue on batch BATCH5 affecting thermal/PCIe resiliency under sustained load. Recommended RMA for affected serials. Also check power-rail connectors."

jon: Action items (short):
- Collect full serial list for all impacted GPUs (maya)
- Start RMA with vendor and request advanced replacement (alex)
- Run canary FW rollback on 1 node and report (suhas)
- Schedule bulk drain windows and migrate jobs to spare pool (ops-oncall)
- Add an automated daily job to snapshot ECC counters per GPU and alert on >200 delta/24h (jon)

maya: I'll post serials in the ticket and attach logs. Also proposed we add a per-rack policy in the console to auto-fallback jobs to dedicated pool when Xid rate exceeds threshold (policy PR incoming).

suhas: One more: run physical inspection for midplane connectors on racks 14-16 — vendor notes loose connectors can amplify flakiness.

ops-oncall: Noted. Physical check scheduled 2026-03-20 09:00 PST with datacenter tech.

jon: Longer-term: inventory shows ~45 cards from BATCH5 across clusters. We should map exposure and decide replacement cadence vs staged RMA (cost vs outage tradeoff).

alex: I'll estimate replacement cost + expedited shipping and post in the finance channel.

maya: TL;DR status: probable bad batch (BATCH5) with some FW interaction. Immediate: drain noisy nodes, RMA affected serials, canary rollback test, increase monitoring.

jon: :thumbsup: keep updates here. I'll draft a short postmortem template for the cluster post-RMA (root cause, detection, mitigation, follow-ups).

maya: Adding folks to the ticket and updating runbook. Thanks all.

infra-bot: thread closed (auto) — no new alerts for 24h after drain + RMA schedule
